newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: American reappointed U.N. food aid chief.
newsitem.headline: American reappointed U.N. food aid chief.

text.p: Catherine Bertini, an American, has been reappointed executive director of the Rome-based World Food Programme (WFP) for another five years, the United Nations announced on Tuesday.
Bertini has a budget of $1.2 billion and a staff of more than 4,000 to combat hunger in developing nations and help design programmes to prevent food shortages.
A former U.S. assistant secretary of agriculture, Bertini, from New York state, first assumed her post in 1992 after being proposed by former President George Bush.
Several Republican congressmen, particularly Benjamin Gilman of New York, urged U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan in January to make sure she would continue in the job, U.N. sources said.
The WFP has been involved in providing emergency food to North Korea, and Bertini plans to visit Pyongyang on March 15 to assess the country's food needs.
